So the receiver always fell through to Bearer auth and the request had no Bearer header to validate against. Cross-node peer forwarding was effectively dead unless both daemons happened to use the same generated key. Fix: changed signature to take `auth_header: Option<&str>`, callers in chat_completions extract original Authorization from request headers and forward verbatim. In the standard cluster deployment all daemons share an admin-set API key, so the receiver's Bearer check passes; unauthed local probes still fail (correct).

R65 #5 — Agent flagged dispatch dropping PoolMessage::JoinRequest signature with `signature: _`. After tracing the actual security model: the signature is over (code_hash, requester_node_id) signed by the requester's identity key, but transport-level gossip_seal already proves sender ownership of the same private key, and dispatch line 860 enforces `requester == sender` from the transport-authenticated envelope. The signature provides no defense beyond what (transport auth + requester==sender) already provide. The actual replay risk (eavesdropper extracts code_hash from sealed gossip and constructs JoinRequest{H, attacker, sig_attacker(H, attacker)}) is NOT prevented by re-verifying the signature — attacker signs their own (H, attacker) pair with their own key and the sig validates. Real fix would be to bind code_hash to the original code preimage (e.g. include code text in the JoinRequest, hash on receive). Logged as wontfix because the agent's recommended fix (verify signature) doesn't actually prevent the attack they described, and the deeper protocol change is out of scope for a sweep round. Documented for future protocol revision.

R65 #6 — handle_credit_forward persisted to TREE_POOL_FORWARDS dedup audit log first (line 729), then called apply_credit_direct(...Earning) (line 735). R66 #3 — evaluate() emitted cycle_complete activity event on every call, including no-op cycles. The notify path bypasses the 60s cooldown when has_p2p_failures=true, so a 50-shard burst of HF download completions could fire 50 cycle_complete events in seconds. activity_tx capacity is 256; combined with 150+ per-shard events, a cold-start burst could saturate the channel and drop events from other subsystems. Gated emission on `delta != 0 || new_downloads > 0` — silent no-op cycles no longer fire the bus.

R66 #4 — Config::validate() didn't bound-check inference.swift_skip_ratio (valid 0.0-0.95) or inference.cross_node_prefix_trust_min (valid 0.0-1.0). swift_skip_ratio >= 1.0 would zero-divide / produce empty layer ranges in the SWIFT draft pass. cross_node_prefix_trust_min outside [0,1] silently trusts everyone or no one. Added explicit bounds checks with SwarmError::Config and clear messages explaining what each value controls and the failure mode.

R66 #5 — init_tracing() read logging.level from `dirs::data_dir().join('swarmllm').join('config.toml')` — the hardcoded platform default — instead of the data dir resolved by SWARMLLM_NODE_DATA_DIR. A user running node2 with SWARMLLM_NODE_DATA_DIR=/tmp/node2 silently got node1's config (or 'info' fallback), violating the documented env > default precedence. Switched to `swarmllm::config::resolve_data_dir(None)` so the env var is respected. CLI --data-dir isn't available pre-parsing — accepted limitation.

R66 #6 — Five CLI client subcommands (Status, Chat, Peers, Bench, Pool) hardcoded `cli.port.unwrap_or(8800)` — fully ignoring SWARMLLM_NODE_LISTEN_PORT despite docs claiming env > default precedence. A user running their daemon on a non-default port via env var would have CLI clients silently connect to 8800 and fail. Added `resolve_client_port` helper and replaced all five sites; precedence now correctly: CLI flag > SWARMLLM_NODE_LISTEN_PORT env > 8800.

R66 #7 — verify_balance_report's future-timestamp check (added in R65 with CLOCK_SKEW_TOLERANCE_SECS = 30) had no test. Added two complementary tests: `future_dated_report_rejected` (60s in future, well beyond skew, must Err) and `slightly_future_report_accepted_within_skew_tolerance` (5s in future, within 30s skew, must Ok). Brings the 5-min one-sided staleness contract under explicit test coverage.

R66 #8 — register_and_lookup_background_state inserts into the process-global BACKGROUND_STATE static DashMap and removes via async deregister_background_stream at the end. A panic anywhere between insert and the cleanup-await would leak the entry into the static, potentially affecting later tests in the same process. Added a BgStateTestGuard RAII struct with sync Drop impl that does BACKGROUND_STATE.remove() + unregister_background_cancel(). Cleanup now panic-safe.

R66 #9 — kv_cache TTL margin tests had only ~9-10ms safety headroom (TTL=1ms+sleep=10ms, TTL=50ms+sleep=30+30ms). On shared CI runners, OS scheduler jitter above the headroom could flake. Increased to 10x margin (session_expires + cleanup_removes_expired: TTL=10ms, sleep=100ms; touch_refreshes_ttl: TTL=200ms, sleeps=120+120ms) — same semantics, robust under load.
R66 #10 — cleanup_removes_old_entries had window=1ms+sleep=5ms (4ms headroom). Increased to window=10ms+sleep=100ms (10x margin). Same as R66 #9.

R66 #11 — spawn_test_server used a fixed `tokio::time::sleep(50ms)` to wait for the Axum server to bind, applied to every integration test. On slow CI runners 50ms could be insufficient (spurious ConnectionRefused); on fast machines it was wasted time. Replaced with a TCP probe loop: try connect to the bound port with 1ms backoff, 2s deadline. Passes 22/22 integration tests faster + more robust.

R66 — schedule_acquisition_cleanup uses bare tokio::spawn (9 callers across 6 files). Refactor to BackgroundTasks JoinSet would require threading shutdown_rx through every caller. Risk-reward not worth it for a 5s sleep + DashMap::remove with no panic surface. Logged for tracking; not changing.

R66 — TpAllReduce all-partials-arrived branch uses bare tokio::spawn to avoid blocking the dispatch loop on ntx.send().await. Pattern is correct (gotcha #11) but spawned task isn't tracked. The reduce_sum + send loop is microseconds; risk of orphan task leak operationally low. Logged for tracking; not changing.

R66 — last_rebalance_per_model keyed by ModelId, not ShardId. Multiple under-replicated shards in same model only get one cooldown. Behavior change to dedup logic is risk > reward without seeing this fire in the wild. Logged for tracking; needs measurement before changing.

R67 #1 — DSD expected_kv_len initialized to `prompt_token_count + 1` while the canonical Item 2 path (speculative.rs:205) uses `prompt_token_count`. Both call forward_through_segments with seq_num=0 for prefill which writes KV for prompt_token_count positions; the sampled first_token isn't yet in remote KV. The +1 caused new_expected_kv vs kv_after_forward arithmetic to drift on partial-accept rounds, leaving stale KV positions that produced silently-wrong attention output without an error. Aligned to the speculative.rs baseline + added a comment explaining why.

R67 #2 — Both DSD and Item 2 spec_logits guards used `< drafts.len()` (γ) but greedy_accept_reject indexes `spec_logits[drafts.len()]` on the ALL-ACCEPTED branch — that's index γ requiring length γ+1. A response with exactly γ rows (corruption / shape mismatch on the worker) would pass the guard then OOB-panic in greedy_accept_reject. Tightened both guards to `< drafts.len() + 1` with an explanatory comment.

R67 #3 — pending_vision_results.insert(request_id, ...) silently overwrites a live waiter on a request_id collision (UUID collision is near-zero, but a request_id reused across a crashed/timed-out session that didn't unregister IS possible). The original waiter's tx is lost and that task hangs forever on rx. Switched to entry().or_insert() pattern: collision returns SwarmError::Internal explicitly rather than silently overwriting.

R67 #4 — On Unix, identity key was written via OpenOptions+write_all without a subsequent sync_all(). A kernel panic / power loss between write_all returning and the page cache flushing leaves a 0-byte file on disk; load_or_generate then errors with 'Invalid key file size: 0 bytes' and the node permanently can't start under its existing identity. Added file.sync_all() right after write_all on the Unix branch — cheap insurance for a 32-byte write.

R67 #5 — node_stats.requests_served and node_stats.forwards_served were updated via `try_write()` which silently drops the increment under contention. Dashboard, MCP tools, WebSocket stats_update, admin /api/admin/stats, and pool DeviceStats all read these fields as authoritative — counts under-reported during inference bursts. Added requests_served_atomic + forwards_served_atomic AtomicU64 fields on MetricsProviders. Updated 3 write sites (dispatch::track_forward_participation, distributed_exec, pipeline/local) to fetch_add and 5 read sites (admin.rs, websocket.rs, mcp/tools.rs, pool/manager/gossip.rs) to load. NodeStats RwLock kept for fields that don't have the contention problem (uptime_start, requests_made which is only API-side).

R67 #6 — `tracing::error!(... 'DIAG: execute_request failed: {e}')` embedded the error in the message string via {e} format. Other error sites in the codebase use `error = %e` as a structured field for log-aggregator queryability. Switched to the structured form.

R67 #7 — DIAGNOSTICS.md WS table documented `DIAG: websocket connected` with `addr` field, but actual code emits `DIAG: client connected` with `subsystem = websocket` field (and no addr). R67 #8 — TREE_POOL_FORWARDS append-only audit/dedup log had no pruning. At steady state with 60 forwards/min × pool size, growth is ~hundreds of MB/day forever. Added prune_pool_forwards_older_than(cutoff) using db.iter_json + db.remove; spawn_responses_sweep tick now prunes entries older than 30 days. Dedup window only needs to outlive the per-member rate-limit window (60s); 30 days is conservative protection.

R67 — Agent claimed `r.clone()` on a DashMap Ref holds the lock across awaits. False alarm: dashmap::mapref::one::Ref does NOT impl Clone in dashmap 6.x; `r.clone()` resolves via Deref<Target=V> to V::clone, releases the Ref at end-of-expression. Same pattern used in 5+ other call sites without issue. Skipped — wontfix.

R67 — Agent flagged keep-session-on-disconnect-during-active-pipeline as a nonce desync risk if remote also moves to new session.
